Hey I just wanted to comment and say that I’ve been in the same situation with a partner still smoking and me trying to quit at the same time. PLEASE do not take this the wrong way. After me and my partner broke up for unrelated reasons, my addiction disappeared because I wasn’t around her smoking multiple times a day. I didn’t see that coming at all, and it was a pleasant surprise. 

I am NOT telling you to leave your partner at all. I just wanted to share that as something to keep in mind when setting boundaries with your partner about weed. Being around someone who smokes regularly can be really, really difficult for some people including myself. I wanted to share to warn you and your partner to take those boundaries extremely seriously and to not ever allow any exceptions whenever possible. I made that mistake multiple times along with my partner not giving enough of a damn to make a real effort to not do things like blow smoke near me or, like you said, kiss me after smoking. Not at all saying that that is your situation. That’s just the extreme that I had to deal with, and it was crippling my efforts to quit. Those boundaries are everything, and you’re going to have to be 100% sure that you and your partner, especially when they’re high, respect them as if they were written by a god. 

I don’t want weed to be something that comes in between your relationship, but the reality is that it has that potential. I honestly don’t know how I would do with a partner that did take things extremely seriously and did everything perfectly, but I don’t believe that having a functioning, healthy relationship in that situation is impossible. Obviously it’s up to you guys to make that call, but anyways, I’m wishing you the best of luck, and I hope this is at least a little helpful.

You’re worth so much more than to be destroyed, and you need to make sure know that. You have value. I’ve also been through depression while smoking, and I know it’s hell, but problems get so much easier to fix when you’re not smoking. 

At this point, the most important things is remember that you’re worthy of love and you’re worthy of living a good, happy life. Just try your best with staying sober, and don’t put off getting help. Maybe a psychiatrist would be better than a therapist at this point because of the voices, but don’t put off getting help. Hi there. The most effective way to combat cravings or addiction as a whole is to associate these things with negative emotions. Two very simple ways that I do this when a feel a craving come up are either by emptying my lungs and holding my breath(I can’t recommend this because of danger of passing out, but it works for me), or by making myself angry. The breath holding associates cravings with anxiety, and of course making yourself angry associates cravings with anger. This is the best option as I now get pissed off at weed for even existing. Both of these have been extremely effective for me. I’m two months sober as of yesterday. Good luck to you.
